mandatory_pre_source.order: Read this whole correction before any earlier alternating source body cited for historical context; it does not add any premise to the independent Jordan proof.

primary.exact_statement: For prime r>7 and integer t with 3<=t<r, set n=r+t and D=n/gcd(n,t!). If D>7, then there do not exist three proper subgroups of A_n whose three pairwise index gcds are all <=7. In particular direct P7 is excluded and Sun8 holds for actual pairwise disjoint left cosets in this stated family, conditional on the named Jordan theorem.
primary.required_source_import: Gareth A. Jones, arXiv:1209.5169v1, Theorem 1.1: a finite primitive degree-n permutation group containing a prime-length cycle fixing at least three points contains A_n.
primary.source_proof_scope: The classical theorem statement is imported, not proved or independently verified; standard Sylow, elementary blocks, set-stabilizer and alternating-group facts are also used. No A_r unique-overgroup, Sun7, R8, external-model, human, formal or novelty finding is imported.
derivation_to_review: t<r implies n<2r, Sylow r is one actual r-cycle and r-free index implies the subgroup contains such a cycle.

If that subgroup were transitive and imprimitive, the r-cycle acts trivially on fewer than r blocks, so its whole support lies in one block of size >=r, forcing n>=2r; hence transitive implies primitive.
The actual cycle fixes t>=3 points, so Jordan forces a transitive subgroup to contain A_n and hence equal A_n, contrary to properness.
For an intransitive subgroup the orbit containing the r moved points has complement 1<=u<=t. The actual alternating set-stabilizer index is binom(n,u), and n/gcd(n,t!) divides that binomial.
Among three pairwise gcd<=7 indices at most one is r-divisible; two r-free indices share D>7, contradiction. Eight disjoint cosets necessarily use proper subgroups.
